summary: Iteration 44: Tested paid Profile Views and Secret Crush (free users see counts only) and AI profile activity. Backend: 11/12 pytest pass. 1 test fails on purpose and shows a real bug: the AI activity skips users whose gender is stored as 'Male'. Passed: POST /profile/{id}/view now stores viewed_user_id and the count goes up. For a free owner, /profile-viewers returns viewers [] with correct total and today counts, and no viewer id or name appears anywhere in the response. Free owner's notification reads 'Kisi ne tumhari profile dekhi...', routes to /likes and has no viewer_id. Premium owner gets the full list, one entry per viewer, newest first, and the notification has the viewer's name and id. Incognito viewers are not stored. Crush with flag off -> 403 'paused'; flag on but non-premium -> 403 'Premium required to send crush'; female/premium -> crush_sent; repeat crush -> 400. Free /crushes -> {crushes:[], total:1}; premium -> full data with revealed true. Ran _run_ai_profile_activity directly with time set to 13:30 IST, random patched, and FCM stubbed: it sets ai_visit_day and ai_visit_target (1-3), the visit count reaches the target and never goes over it in 6 runs, visitors are distinct female AI or auto_chat accounts, and there is exactly 1 AI crush (6-day cap) with last_ai_crush_at set. The live background loop also ran during testing (log: 'AI activity: 2 profile visits'). Frontend at 390x844: a free male sees crush-locked-card (count 1) and viewers-locked-card (count 3) with no names leaked, and both 'Reveal with Premium' buttons go to /premium. A premium male sees the crush card with name and photo and 4 viewer cards (one came from the live AI loop). Discover crush button: it NEVER shows for non-admin users (see the integration issue below), so the non-premium crush -> toast + /premium path was only checked by reading the code.

critical.issue: Uses exact gender matches: 'gender': 'male' for targets and 'female' for visitors. The DB has 3 real users with 'Male' (including Shivamkks122) and auto_chat accounts with 'Female', and these are silently skipped. The rest of server.py matches with {'$regex':'^male$','$options':'i'}. Test test_ai_activity_capitalized_male fails because of this.

minor.issue: The 'Already marked as crush' check (400) runs before the premium check. target_user_id is not checked to exist, and the endpoint has no auth (anyone can send a crush as any user_id).
No auth or ownership check. Anyone can pass a premium user's id and get that user's full viewer and crusher list. The paywall is enforced by the owner's premium status, not by who is asking.

Returns viewer names and photos with NO premium check (data comes from users.profile_viewers, filled by /user/{id}/track-view). The /profile-viewers page (ProfileViewersPage, linked from Privacy settings) uses it, so this is a possible paywall bypass. Right now no frontend code calls track-view, so it is mostly empty. Either gate it or remove it.

integration_issues.issue: DiscoverPage fetches GET /api/admin/feature-flags, which requires an admin (401 without a token, 403 'Admin access required' for a normal premium user). So crushEnabled is always false for non-admin users and the crush button never shows, even when crush_feature=true. Add a public endpoint (e.g. GET /api/feature-flags/public returning crush_feature) or include the flag in /api/init.

No frontend code calls POST /api/profile/{id}/view (UserProfilePage only does GET /profile/{id}). So real views are never recorded; only AI activity creates profile_views. Call the view endpoint with viewer_id when a user opens someone's profile.

action_items: Use case-insensitive gender matching in _run_ai_profile_activity for both target males and female visitors
Expose crush_feature to non-admin users (public flags endpoint or /init) so the Discover crush button can show
Call POST /api/profile/{id}/view?viewer_id=me from UserProfilePage (and wherever a profile is opened) so real views are tracked
Put a premium gate on (or remove) the legacy GET /api/user/{id}/profile-viewers used by ProfileViewersPage
Optional: check auth/ownership on /profile-viewers, /crushes, /crush; check that the target exists; run the premium check before the duplicate check
critical_code_review_comments: _record_profile_view runs `if True:`, which is dead scaffolding. It also sends an FCM push for every AI visit (1-3 pushes a day per user); check this matches the intended notification volume.

In _run_ai_profile_activity the AI crush chance is 0.06 per run x ~28 runs a day, so a crush comes almost surely within about 1 day after the 6-day cooldown (about 1 per 6-7 days). OK, but the loop scans up to 2000 users with per-user DB queries every 30 min, so consider batching.
get_crushes: the else branch (premium_locked) can no longer be reached because free users return early. Remove it.

success_rate.frontend: Likes page 100%; Discover crush button not reachable for non-admin users

seed_data_creation: Temp users (test_tag iter44/iter44b/iter44ui) and their profile_views, crushes and notifications were created and all deleted. crush_feature was set back to false (its original value). The AI activity test used a fake date in 2027, so no real users were touched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_iter44_paid_views_crush.py. The fixture creates and cleans temp users and restores crush_feature. UI: python tests/iter44_ui_seed.py create|cleanup makes test_iter44ui_free@example.com and test_iter44ui_prem@example.com (pw TestIter44@2026). Set crush_feature in Mongo yourself if needed and restore it after. Close the daily reward modal with [data-testid=close-daily-reward]. Playwright page.route could not mock /api/admin/feature-flags (probably a service worker), so to test the crush button you need the backend fix.
